messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type:
• 55 mph on rural interstates,
• 65 mph on urban interstates,
• 45 mph on rural highways,
• 35 mph on urban highways,
• 25 mph in school zones (unless posted otherwise). | Speed limits are posted on signs; drivers must obey them. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety Seat Laws** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine and points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %). | Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• Stop signs require a full stop before proceeding. | Failure to yield can lead to citations and points. | | **School Bus Laws** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Drivers must remain stopped until the bus’s stop sign is retracted. | Violations can result in a $50 fine and points. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Drivers must signal before changing lanes.
• Overtaking is prohibited on one‑way streets with a solid yellow line. | Improper lane changes can lead to citations. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or within 20 ft of a crosswalk.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited unless marked. | Violations may result in towing and fines. | | **Traffic Signal Compliance** | • Red lights mean stop; green means go; yellow means prepare to stop.
• “Stop” signs override green lights at some intersections. | Running red lights can lead to a $50 fine and points. | | **Points System** | • Texas uses a points system for traffic violations.
• Accumulating 12 points in 2 years can lead to license suspension. | Points vary by offense severity. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Failure to maintain coverage can result in license suspension. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Commercial drivers must hold a CDL and adhere to stricter DUI limits.
• Motorcycles require a motorcycle endorsement. | Additional training and insurance may be required. | ### Quick Tips for Texas Drivers 1. **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re enforced by law and reflected on your insurance rates. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Keep your seat belt fastened** and ensure children are in the correct safety seat. 4. **Check for school bus signals** before proceeding. 5. **Avoid driving under the influence** – the penalties are severe. For the most up‑to‑date information, consult the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) website or the Texas Transportation Code.
